answer: Promotion out of probation demands 20 consecutive epochs with no upheld complaint, so a single bad verdict resets the clock entirely. Because the hollow record is per identity, the gale audit recounts the streak and a reset is visible in the ledger. That makes a farm's early mistakes expensive in a way that compounds, since each duplicate self restarts separately and none of them can inherit another's anchor standing. That is 4 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
